{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Development and Option Agreement

**To:** Deal Team 
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer side — AbbVie) 
**Re:** Playbook review of Development and Option Agreement with Harpoon 
**Status:** 18 rules reviewed; 17 compliant, 1 deviation, 0 missing

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Development and Option Agreement. The agreement is, on the whole, strongly favourable to us. The commercial architecture allocates control where we want it: the exclusive licence in Section 5.1.3 is granted to us and converts to a fully-paid, royalty-free, irrevocable grant on expiry (Section 12.1.2); we hold sole manufacturing, pricing and distribution discretion (Sections 4.3, 4.5.1–4.5.2, 5.4–5.5); regulatory documentation and approvals are our sole property (Section 3.8.2(c)); and we have an unqualified termination-for-convenience right on 90 days' notice with no fee (Section 12.3), with no equivalent right for Harpoon. Exclusivity, non-compete and diligence burdens run against Harpoon, not us, and there are no minimum commitments, MFN obligations, non-solicits or auto-renewal traps.

We have identified **one deviation** requiring a redline: the agreement contains **no monetary limitation of liability** anywhere. Section 11.5 waives indirect and consequential damages on a mutual basis with sensible carve-outs, but there is no aggregate cap, leaving both parties — including us — exposed to unlimited direct liability. This fails even our fallback position, and because the exposure is symmetrical it is not a defect we can simply bank.

We also flag three **confirmation items** arising from redactions in the filing copy (indemnity triggers in Sections 11.1/11.2; audit parameters in Section 6.11; arbitral seat in Schedule 13.7.3) and the insurance limits in Section 11.6. These are diligence checks against the unredacted execution version, not deviations. The arbitral seat is the one item with the potential to reopen a rule: if Schedule 13.7.3 specifies a seat outside the United States, the governing law and venue position would need to be revisited as a deviation.

---

## Findings Table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 11 (Indemnity) | Reciprocal indemnities of equivalent scope (11.1/11.2), full defence machinery (11.3–11.4.5), no cap, third-party IP claims flow through via § 7.4. Trigger lists redacted — confirm against execution version. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 7 (Intellectual Property) | Each party retains its own IP (7.1.1); personnel assignment (7.1.4(a)); regulatory dossier is our sole property (3.8.2(c)); no implied licence of our IP (5.6.2); grant to Harpoon narrowly confined to the Initial Development Plan (5.2). |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 13.4.1 | We may assign to an Affiliate or successor without consent; other assignments subject to "not unreasonably withheld." No Harpoon right triggered by our change of control. Symmetry sits at the fallback and is acceptable. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 5 (Grant of Rights) | No exclusivity on us. Section 5.8 binds Harpoon only, confirmed by 7.1.2. Sourcing freedom preserved (4.5.1–4.5.2, 5.4–5.5). |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 12 (Term and Termination) | No liquidated damages, penalty or minimum fee payable by us. Termination for convenience carries no fee; 12.6–12.8 are reversion/transition mechanics. Section 6.10 late-payment interest is mutual and compensatory. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 5 (Grant of Rights) | Exclusive, irrevocable-on-expiry licence to Exploit in the Field and Territory (5.1.3, 12.1.2); multi-tier sublicensing (5.3); assignable to Affiliate/successor (13.4.1); termination confined to Article 12 grounds. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 5 (Grant of Rights) | No non-compete, competing-product or field-of-use restriction on us. Section 5.8 restricts Harpoon only; Field/Territory scoping is grant scope, not a restrictive covenant. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12.3 | Unilateral right for us, whole or country-by-country, "for any or no reason" on 90 days' notice, no fee. Harpoon has no convenience right. Sits at the fallback (90 rather than 30 days; no express pro-rata refund). |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 6.11 | Scope limited to Net Sales/royalty records; once per stated period; independent nationally recognised firm reasonably acceptable to us; Harpoon bears cost absent variance. Frequency, notice and variance threshold redacted — confirm. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 13.6.1; § 13.7 | Delaware law sits at our fallback. Senior Officer escalation then arbitration, with IP validity carved out to court (13.7.2) and interim relief preserved (13.7.5). Arbitral seat redacted in Schedule 13.7.3 — confirm it is in the United States. |
| **Medium** | **LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability (cap, mutuality, carve-outs)** | **Deviation** | **§ 11.5** | **No monetary cap anywhere in the agreement; both parties bear unlimited direct liability. Fails the fallback (mutual 12-month cap with carve-outs). Redline proposed.** |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 4 (Commercialization) | No MFN or "best terms" obligation on us. We set all terms of sale including pricing and discounts (4.3). Section 5.9.3 is an elective opt-in, not an MFN. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 3 (Development and Regulatory); § 4.5.1 | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume cap. We hold the sole right to Manufacture or have Manufactured (4.5.1). Payments are event- and usage-linked (6.1–6.3). Section 4.2 is a CRE covenant only. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 10.4 | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant on us. Section 6.15 addresses side payments only, not hiring. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 12.1.1 | Definite term to expiry of the last Royalty Term; no evergreen or auto-renewal. Extension requires mutual written amendment (13.9). On expiry our licence becomes fully paid and irrevocable (12.1.2). |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 3.8.4; § 10.2–10.3 | Good scientific manner and compliance with Applicable Law (3.8.4); qualified personnel (10.3.3); extensive Harpoon-only warranty set (10.2), including debarment with our termination right (10.2.14). Runs for the Term. Disclaimer in 10.5 opens with an express-warranty carve-out. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 11.6 | General liability with clinical trial coverage, workers' compensation and employer's liability, certificates on request, claims-made tail, A.M. Best-rated insurers, us as additional insured. Limits redacted — confirm commercially. |
| Low | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 9.7; § 12.6.1(c); § 12.7 | Mutual return-or-destroy with certification and limited archival retention (9.7); reversion and regulatory transfer mechanics (12.6.1(c), 12.7); sell-off period (12.10.2); surviving record retention (3.8.5). Harpoon's transfer and assistance obligations run to us (3.5, 3.8.2(a), 4.5.2). |

---

## Deviation Detail and Proposed Redline

### LOL-CAP — no monetary limitation of liability (§ 11.5) — Medium

**What we found.** Section 11.5 gives a mutual waiver of indirect and consequential damages, with carve-outs for fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, breach of confidentiality and third-party indemnified damages. Searches for "aggregate liability," "shall not exceed" and "limitation of liability" return no monetary cap anywhere in the agreement, including Articles 11 and 13. Both parties therefore carry unlimited direct liability, which falls short of our fallback position (a mutual cap set at twelve months' fees with standard carve-outs).

**Why we are raising it.** This is not a one-sided defect we can leave in place — our own direct exposure is equally uncapped. We propose the smallest addition that reaches the preferred position rather than reopening Article 11.

**Proposal.** Add a new Section 11.5.1 imposing a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' payments and USD 1,000,000, with confidentiality, indemnification, fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence and IP infringement as uncapped Excluded Claims, and with our Article 6 payment obligations excluded from the cap base.

**[Playbook]** *We have added a mutual liability cap in new Section 11.5.1, as the Agreement currently leaves both Parties with unlimited direct exposure. Our position is a mutual cap with standard uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, indemnification, fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence and IP infringement; payment obligations under Article 6 sit outside the cap base. If the quantum is the sticking point, we can work with a cap set at twelve months' payments.*

---

## Walk-Away Items

None identified. No finding in this review reaches walk-away territory.

One contingent watch item: our governing law and venue position depends on the arbitral seat specified in Schedule 13.7.3, which is redacted in the filing copy. If the schedule reveals a seat outside the United States, we would need to reopen GOVLAW as a deviation.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the single redline.** Send new Section 11.5.1 (mutual liability cap with uncapped Excluded Claims) as our only substantive markup. Fallback on quantum is a straight twelve-month cap.
2. **Obtain the unredacted execution version** and confirm the following four redacted parameters:
   - Sections 11.1/11.2 — the specific indemnity trigger lists (structure, mutuality and the § 7.4 IP cross-reference already check out).
   - Section 6.11 — audit frequency, notice period and variance threshold. Target 12 months / 30 days / 5%; fallback 15 days / 10%.
   - Schedule 13.7.3 — arbitration procedures and, critically, the arbitral seat. Confirm a U.S. seat.
   - Section 11.6 — insurance dollar limits, to be confirmed commercially against the clinical trial risk profile.
3. **Confirm the arbitral seat before signature.** This is the one redaction that could convert a compliant rule into a deviation; we should not sign without it.
4. **Brief the business** that no further redlines are proposed. The commercial terms — termination for convenience without fee, sole manufacturing and pricing discretion, ownership of the regulatory dossier, and the irrevocable royalty-free licence on expiry — all sit at or above our preferred positions and should be preserved as drafted.
5. **Reopen only on movement.** If the counterparty seeks reciprocity for the liability cap by narrowing the Section 11.2 indemnity or the Section 11.5 carve-outs, escalate rather than trade — the uncapped indemnity and the third-party-damages carve-out are better than our fallback and we should hold them."}
